task_name: World 133 Task B  -  S-Corp 60/40 Pro-Rata Distribution Equalization, Shareholder Loan Split, Zero-W2 Officer Risk & Stock Basis Excess
prompt: Using the shareholder ownership, W-2, Corporate Bylaws, and stock-basis schedule alongside the October 2026 checking and corporate Amex ledger for Crestline Specialty Contracting Inc. in scorp_oct2026_owner_draws_personal_card_and_equity.xlsx, determine how each shareholder's personal charges and unsubstantiated withdrawals must be recorded on the Balance Sheet without violating S-corporation single-class-of-stock pro-rata distribution rules, evaluate Officer W-2 reasonable compensation compliance, and compute any shareholder YTD distribution-in-excess-of-basis exposure.

rubric.description: Demonstrates that booking all $24,200.00 (SH-A) and $3,800.00 (SH-B) directly to shareholder distributions on top of $15,000.00 and $10,000.00 cash distributions would yield $39,200.00 (73.96%) vs $13,800.00 (26.04%) on $53,000.00 total, violating the executed 60%/40% Corporate Bylaws (Section 7.4) and requiring corrective equalization under NOTE-2026-A to align with governing pro-rata stock rights.

Applies Section 7.4 Corporate Bylaws (NOTE-2026-A) by matching Shareholder B's $3,800.00 (40%) to establish an incremental 60%/40% pro-rata distribution pool of $9,500.00 ($5,700.00 to 3310 Distributions - Shareholder A and $3,800.00 to 3320 Distributions - Shareholder B).

Records Shareholder A's non-pro-rata excess of $18,500.00 ($24,200.00 less $5,700.00 pro-rata distribution slice) as a formal receivable Dr 1380 Due from Shareholder A $18,500.00 under promissory note NOTE-2026-A.
Verifies audited October 2026 cumulative distributions of $20,700.00 in 3310 (60.00%) and $13,800.00 in 3320 (40.00%) totaling $34,500.00, preserving exact 60.00% / 40.00% pro-rata parity.

Flags critical IRS reasonable-compensation payroll tax exposure on active full-time officer Elena Rostova (SH-B, 45 hrs/wk VP Field Ops) receiving $0.00 YTD W-2 wages while taking $77,800.00 in YTD S-corp distributions.
Computes Shareholder B's pre-distribution stock basis ceiling as $70,000.00 ($58,000.00 Jan 1, 2026 stock basis + $12,000.00 allocable YTD net income share, with $0.00 shareholder loan basis).

Computes Shareholder B's audited YTD distributions through 2026-10-31 as $77,800.00 ($64,000.00 prior Jan-Sep + $13,800.00 audited October) and identifies $7,800.00 of distributions in excess of stock basis taxable as capital gain under IRC Section 1368(b)(2) with $0.00 ending stock basis.

Places a named close/tax governance hold (scorp_pro_rata_and_reasonable_comp_hold) preventing final tax/equity certification until W-2 officer payroll, Box 1 medical inclusion, and NOTE-2026-A repayment terms are attested.
